rules.title: NJ Anti-Eviction Act: enumerated grounds and notices to quit (subsections (l)-(r))
rules.requirement: A landlord may evict only for statutory causes. Examples: owner or buyer personal occupancy (2 months' notice to quit, no suit until the lease expires), end of employment-based tenancy (3 days), drug, assault or theft convictions (3 days), and human trafficking.
rules.quoted_span: A Notice to Quit must be served on the tenant three days prior to filing a suit for eviction (N.J.S.A. 2A:18-61.1(m)).
rules.key_value: Notice to quit: 2 months (owner/buyer occupancy), 3 days (employment ended, convictions)
rules.exemptions: Owner-occupied two- and three-family dwellings are governed by N.J.S.A. 2A:18-61.2.

rules.title: NJ evictions in owner-occupied two- and three-family dwellings
rules.requirement: Tenants in owner-occupied two- or three-family homes can be removed only by court order, and only for listed causes such as holdover or nonpayment. Notice to quit: 3 months for at-will or year-to-year tenancies, 1 month for month-to-month, and 3 days for disorderly conduct, damage or rule violations.
rules.quoted_span: Tenants of landlord-occupied two- and three-family dwellings can be removed only when a court issues an order for eviction.
rules.key_value: 3-month / 1-month / 3-day notice to quit depending on tenancy type and cause

rules.title: NJ Anti-Eviction Act penalties for misuse of removal notices
rules.requirement: If a landlord says it will occupy a unit or remove the building from residential use and then does not follow through, the former tenant can recover treble damages plus fees. Owner occupancy must last at least 6 months, and a removed building must stay out of residential use for 5 years. A civil penalty of up to $10,000 per violation can also apply.
rules.quoted_span: the landlord must not use this property for residential use for a period of five (5) years.
rules.key_value: 3x damages plus fees; up to $10,000 civil penalty per violation
rules.penalty: Three times damages plus attorney fees and costs; civil penalty up to $10,000 per violation

rules.title: NJ tenant reprisal protection
rules.requirement: A landlord cannot evict, substantially change lease terms, or refuse to renew in retaliation for a tenant exercising protected rights. These include enforcing lease or legal rights, making good-faith health or safety complaints, and joining a tenant organization. The tenant may sue for damages.
rules.quoted_span: A landlord cannot take reprisal action against a tenant by eviction, substantial alteration of a lease or its terms, or refusal to renew a lease when a tenant exercises certain civil rights (N.J.S.A. 2A:42-10.10).

rules.title: NJ foreclosure: tenants protected from eviction and 90-day notice
rules.requirement: Foreclosure alone is not grounds for eviction. A buyer who wants to occupy the unit as a primary residence must give a 90-day notice to quit, and a longer lease must run out first. New owners must send English and Spanish notices of the change in ownership within 10 business days.
citation_aliases: Chase Manhattan Bank v. Josephson, 135 N.J. 209 (1994)
rules.quoted_span: Foreclosure alone is not grounds for eviction in New Jersey.

rules.title: NJ Senior Citizens and Disabled Protected Tenancy Act (condo/co-op conversion)
rules.requirement: Eligible seniors, disabled tenants, and disabled veterans in buildings being converted to condos or co-ops can be protected from eviction for up to 40 years. They must meet an income limit and apply within the stated period.
citation_aliases: Tenant Protection Act of 1992 (N.J.S.A. 2A:18-61.40 to -61.59, Hudson County)
rules.quoted_span: Tenants may be protected from eviction for 40 years if their family income is not more than three (3) times the average per person income in their county
rules.key_value: Up to 40 years of protected tenancy

requires_unknown_facts: building is being converted to a condominium or cooperative
tenant is a qualifying senior or disabled person

parsed.doc_summary: Part 4 of the NJ DCA Landlord-Tenant guide. It covers Anti-Eviction Act grounds and notices, owner-occupied 2-3 family rules, penalties, reprisal protection, foreclosure tenant protections, and protected tenancy for seniors and disabled tenants. The rest is contact directories. It has no content on rent, deposits, fees, screening or algorithmic pricing.
